title: Kathy Hochul
intro:
Report an officeholder change
Kathy Hochul (Democratic Party) is the Governor of New York. She assumed office on August 24, 2021. Her current term ends on January 1, 2027.
Hochul is the 57th Governor of New York. She assumed office following the resignation of then-Gov. Andrew Cuomo (D). She won a full term as governor in 2022, defeating Lee Zeldin in the general election. Previously, Hochul served as the 77th Lieutenant Governor of New York, a position she was elected to as Cuomo's running mate in 2014 and 2018. She served in the United States House of Representatives from 2011 to 2012 and was Clerk of Erie County from 2007 to 2011. In 2012, challenger Chris Collins (R) defeated Hochul 50.8% to 49.2%.
Hochul announced she would run for re-election in 2026 on July 2, 2024.
In her first term, Hochul approved investments in childcare and public education and signed bills expanding the state's red flag law and limiting the purchase of semiautomatic rifles and body armor. She also signed legislation expanding protections for doctors who prescribe abortion pills, and sped up the planned implementation of a $1.2 billion tax cut.
As governor, Hochul is responsible for appointing judges to the state's appellate courts. In April 2023, Hochul appointed Rowan Wilson as chief judge of the New York Court of Appeals, the state's court of last resort, to replace the retired Janet DiFiore. This appointment shifted the court's majority from conservative to liberal.
In her 2026 state of the state address, Hochul announced a proposal to increase funding for early childhood education and establish universal pre-K for 4-year-olds, as well as plans to amend the state's environmental review processes for housing and infrastructure projects. Following the United States Supreme Court's decision in Louisiana v. Callais, Hochul said the state should amend its redistricting process to draw new congressional maps before the 2030 Census.
